answer:
Use buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam as the solver.
Model the domain as a 2D square cavity with side length L = 1 m in the x-y plane.
Use one cell thickness in the z direction and set the front and back patches to empty.
Use a uniform square mesh with 81 by 81 cells.
Set gravity to (0, -9.81, 0) m/s^2.
Enable the Boussinesq buoyancy approximation.
Set TRef = 295 K.
Set Pr = 0.71.
Set beta = 1/TRef and set nu = sqrt(Pr * g * beta * deltaT * L^3 / Ra) so that Ra = 1e5 for deltaT = 10 K and L = 1 m.
Set the left wall temperature to 300 K with fixedValue.
Set the right wall temperature to 290 K with fixedValue.
Set the top and bottom wall temperature boundary conditions to zeroGradient for adiabatic walls.
Set the velocity boundary condition to noSlip on all walls.
Initialize U to 0, T to 295 K, and p_rgh to 0.
Use zeroGradient for p_rgh on all walls.
Run the simulation to steady state until the residuals for U, p_rgh, and T fall below 1e-6 and the hot-wall Nusselt number stops changing.
Report the hot-wall Nusselt number and compare it with the de Vahl Davis benchmark for Ra = 1e5.
